questions.prompt: Where should you start designing permission tests?
options: From a confirmed permission matrix of roles and actions
questions.explanation: Every cell of the matrix is a test.

questions.prompt: If the Delete button is hidden for Viewers, the Viewer role cannot delete records.
questions.explanation: Hiding a control is not access control. Check the server through the URL or API.

questions.prompt: A customer changes /orders/1001 to /orders/1002 and sees another customer's order. What is this?
options: Horizontal access control failure (insecure direct object reference)
questions.explanation: Same privilege level, different user's data. That is horizontal.

questions.prompt: Which tests belong in a permission test set? Select all that apply.
options: Allowed action by the right role
Denied action by a lower role
Another user's record accessed by a same-role user
Permissions after role change and logout
questions.explanation: Positive, negative, horizontal and post-change tests all belong.

questions.prompt: A logged-in user without permission calls an admin endpoint. Which response is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Authenticated but not authorised gives 403; unauthenticated usually 401.

questions.prompt: An editor is demoted to viewer but keeps editing for an hour. What is likely wrong?
options: Permissions are cached in the session/token and not re-checked after the role change
questions.explanation: Permissions must be re-evaluated after role changes.

questions.prompt: Why do negative permission tests matter more than positive ones for security?
options: Defects usually are users being able to do something they should not, which positive tests never reveal
questions.explanation: Positive tests confirm allowed actions work but do not find over-permission.

questions.prompt: A viewer sends PUT /api/records/7 with a valid token and the record changes, although the UI has no edit button. What do you report?
options: Broken access control at the API: authorisation is enforced only in the UI
questions.explanation: The server is the real boundary, so this is high severity.

questions.prompt: Your matrix has 6 roles and 25 actions. What is the sensible way to test?
options: Confirm the matrix, generate every cell as a test (automated at API level where possible), and prioritise sensitive actions manually
questions.explanation: Every cell is a test, but automation and risk prioritisation keep it feasible.

coding.title: Turn a permission matrix into tests
coding.prompt:
Write `permission_tests(matrix)` that turns a permission matrix into test cases.

`matrix` maps `(role, action)` to `True` (allowed) or `False` (denied). Return a sorted list of `(role, action, expected)` tuples where `expected` is `"allow"` or `"deny"`. **Every cell is a test.**

Then write `negative_tests(matrix)` returning only the denied tests (the `"deny"` ones), keeping the sort order.
coding.explanation: Every (role, action) cell becomes a test with an expected allow or deny. Sorting makes the list stable, and the negative tests are the denied subset, which deserve the most attention for security.
hints: Iterate over `matrix.items()` and build a tuple per cell.
negative_tests can reuse permission_tests and filter on the third item.

tests.name: every cell is a test
tests.code:
perm = {("admin","delete"): True, ("editor","delete"): False, ("viewer","delete"): False, ("admin","edit"): True, ("editor","edit"): True, ("viewer","edit"): False}
t = permission_tests(perm)
assert len(t) == 6
assert t[0] == ("admin", "delete", "allow")

tests.name: expected values
negative tests only
